root_cause.text: f2fs_put_super() in the f2fs unmount path failed to synchronize outstanding node page read I/O before teardown and leak checking, allowing asynchronous F2FS_RD_NODE page references to remain active during superblock shutdown.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “f2fs_put_super() is called before all node page reads are completed,” causing a “filesystem reference count leak during umount, type: 9, count: 1,” and the fix adds waiting for page completion via f2fs_wait_on_all_pages() for F2FS_RD_NODE before the final page-count leak check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the page reference leak BUG check from f2fs unmount to prevent erroneous crash-on-unmount behavior.
intent_record.what: A for-loop in f2fs_put_super() that iterated over all NR_COUNT_TYPE page count types, checked get_pages(sbi, i), logged an error for any nonzero count during unmount, and unconditionally triggered f2fs_bug_on(sbi, 1) was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, unmount will no longer scan page reference counters for leaks at this point, and it will no longer emit an error or force a BUG when any page count remains nonzero, avoiding a crash during unmount based on these checks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an unmount-time check that detects and reports leaked F2FS page reference counts and triggers a bug when any remain.
intent_record.what: A new loop was added in f2fs_put_super() after releasing meta_inode that iterates from 0 to NR_COUNT_TYPE - 1, checks get_pages(sbi, i) for each count type, skips zero counts, logs an error with f2fs_err() when a nonzero page count is found during unmount, and then triggers f2fs_bug_on(sbi, 1).
intent_record.how: At unmount time, after node/meta pages are expected to have been dropped, the filesystem now verifies that all tracked page reference counts are zero. If any count remains nonzero, it reports the leaked count type and value and forces a bug condition, helping detect and stop filesystem reference count leaks instead of silently completing unmount.

The vulnerability involves page references remaining active during f2fs unmount teardown. This change adds an unmount-time check for leaked F2FS page references and bugs out when they remain, directly targeting detection of the exact failure condition caused by the root issue.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is part of the unmount leak-check loop that inspects page reference counts during teardown without first synchronizing outstanding F2FS_RD_NODE read I/O. Because asynchronous node-page reads can still hold references at this point, this check observes transient active references caused by the missing wait in the unmount path.

This BUG assertion turns the unsynchronized outstanding node-page references into a crash during unmount. The root cause is that f2fs_put_super() tears down and performs leak checking before waiting for F2FS_RD_NODE read I/O completion, so this statement is the direct failure point.

Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date:   Sun May 28 15:47:12 2023 +0800

    f2fs: fix to drop all dirty meta/node pages during umount()
    
    For cp error case, there will be dirty meta/node pages remained after
    f2fs_write_checkpoint() in f2fs_put_super(), drop them explicitly, and
    do sanity check on reference count of dirty pages and inflight IOs.
    
    Signed-off-by: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
    Signed-off-by: Jaegeuk Kim <jaegeu
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full unmount teardown sequence, including checkpointing, writeback waits, page leak checking, and final destruction. The root cause is missing synchronization for outstanding node page read I/O before teardown/leak checking. In this snippet, the code waits for discard/writeback only: `f2fs_flush_merged_writes(sbi);` at line 1623 and `f2fs_wait_on_all_pages(sbi, F2FS_WB_CP_DATA);` at line 1625. However, there is no wait for outstanding read I/O on node pages (no synchronization for `F2FS_RD_NODE` before the leak check loop). Immediately after these writeback waits, the code performs leak detection: `for (i = 0; i < NR_COUNT_TYPE; i++) { if (!get_pages(sbi, i)) continue; ... f2fs_bug_on(sbi, 1); }` at lines 1632-1638, and then proceeds with inode/page teardown (`iput(sbi->node_inode)`, `iput(sbi->meta_inode)`, etc.). Because the function lacks a wait for node read I/O completion before this teardown and leak checking, the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present in this version, since the necessary synchronization of outstanding node page read I/O is absent.
